subject: Outbound access: minimal port + FQDN matrix and NAT translation expectations

Subject: Redwood private endpoint — minimal outbound allowlist and NAT behavior

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and NetOps teams are starting the firewall signoff for the Redwood private deployment. To avoid back-and-forth I attached an initial spreadsheet with what we think we need. Before we lock rules, two quick asks:

1) Can you confirm the minimal set of destination FQDNs and IPs we must allow for the control plane and for streaming inference traffic (token responses)?
2) How does Redwood expect TCP vs UDP, specific port ranges, and whether TLS SNI will be stable so we can inspect?
3) If we NAT egress from multiple private subnets (per VPC, per AZ) to a pool of ephemeral outbound IPs, what behaviors should we expect around session affinity and long-lived WebSocket/streaming connections? Any recommendations for NAT timeouts?

Attached: summit-netops-allowlist-reqs.xlsx (our proposed template). We also saw a CSV of Redwood IPs in your docs — can you share the authoritative file for this deployment and state whether it’s stable or subject to rotation?

Would like to get this into our change window next Thursday.

Appreciate the help,
Alex
Network Architect — Summit Health

Subject: Re: Redwood private endpoint — minimal outbound allowlist and NAT behavior

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Looping in Marissa for program/contract context. I also looped Rishi (sec) offline and he prepared the technical sketch below. Quick summary up front: we provide a small set of stable hostnames and a published CSV of egress IPs; we recommend preserving TCP long-lived sessions by aligning NAT timeouts and preserving 1:1 or small pool NAT where possible for streaming use-cases. Details below.

High-level answers:
- Control plane: allow TLS to control.redwood-inference.com and api.redwood-inference.com on TCP 443 (SNI: control.redwood-inference.com / api.redwood-inference.com).
- Streaming / inference responses: connect to stream.redwood-inference.com (TCP 443) — streaming uses WebSocket-over-TLS; SNI is stable.
- Embeddings/other batch endpoints: embed-us.redwood-inference.com (TCP 443).
- IP list: authoritative list attached (redwood-ip-list.csv). We rotate a small fraction of addresses occasionally — we publish a 7-day overlap window when changes occur.

See Rishi’s specific NAT/timeout guidance below.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-ip-list.csv (CSV stub)

On Sun, Aug 30, 2026 at 11:05 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Vanessa/Marissa/Alex — adding technical details for NetOps.
>
> Minimal allowlist (destinations; all outbound TCP 443 unless noted):
> - control.redwood-inference.com (api/control plane) — stable SNI; subject to DNS A-record changes; allow FQDN + IPs in redwood-ip-list.csv
> - api.redwood-inference.com (management API) — TCP 443
> - stream.redwood-inference.com (streaming responses / websockets) — TCP 443; long-lived TLS sessions
> - embed-us.redwood-inference.com (embeddings) — TCP 443
> - metrics-upload.redwood-inference.com (optional, for enhanced telemetry) — TCP 443; may be blocked if you don’t want telemetry
>
> Recommended firewall posture:
> - Prefer FQDN allowlisting at perimeter proxy (if you have an outbound proxy that can resolve/evaluate SNI) + IP backup from redwood-ip-list.csv for firewalls that do not support FQDN rules.
> - Reject outbound to other IPs in the same TLS endpoints unless they match the published CSV.
> - For private deployments in air-gapped or highly regulated environments: use our Private Control Plane option and provide your control-plane CIDR to Redwood for a dedicated peering path (we can discuss offline).
>
> NAT and streaming behavior:
> - WebSocket-over-TLS for streaming creates long-lived, bidirectional connections that rely on TCP state in NAT devices. If your NAT pool rotates IPs mid-session, streams will break.
> - Recommendation 1 (preferred): Reserve a small pool of static outbound IPs (per VPC/AZ) for Redwood egress traffic so streams maintain stable 1:1 or low-ratio NAT mappings. This is the simplest operational model for low reconnection cost.
> - Recommendation 2 (acceptable): If you must use ephemeral NAT, configure NAT port retention and long TCP/TLS session timeouts (idle timeout >= 30 minutes, TCP established timeout >= 120 minutes) to reduce churn for long inference sessions.
> - Session affinity: Where possible, configure sticky NAT based on the source subnet or application tag to keep flows on the same outbound IP during an operation.
> - Keepalive: Use application-level keepalives (WebSocket ping/pong) — Redwood SDKs include a 2-minute keepalive for streaming requests. If your infrastructure terminates idle connections aggressively, reduce the keepalive interval accordingly.
>
> TLS/SNI and inspection:
> - We use TLS 1.3 by default. SNI is stable and can be relied on for hostname-based proxy routing.
> - Deep packet inspection that breaks TLS is not supported; if your proxy performs TLS interception, ensure it presents a hostname-matching certificate chain and is configured to allow WebSocket upgrades.
>
> Operational note on IP rotation:
> - The file redwood-ip-list.csv is authoritative. We issue an announcement on the shared drive and a 7-day overlap where both old and new IPs are in the CSV. If you need a longer freeze window we can negotiate as part of the deployment SLA.
>
> Happy to sync with NetOps on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through NAT behaviour and test a streaming session.
>
> — Rishi
> Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
>

Subject: Re: Redwood private endpoint — minimal outbound allowlist and NAT behavior

Thanks Rishi — that’s very helpful. A couple clarifications from NetOps after reviewing:

- We run egress through a per-VPC NAT gateway that rotates IPs every 6 hours today as part of our autoscaling pattern. We can reserve a /29 (static IPs) for the Redwood subnets but need to confirm cost/approval.
- Our perimeter proxy supports SNI-based rules but does not do TLS interception for customer traffic. Good to know TLS 1.3 + stable SNI are supported.
- One remaining ask: do you provide a dedicated TLS certificate (SAN) for private deployments or should we rely on SNI only? We need to ensure our proxy doesn't try to rewrite hostnames for logging.

We’d like the authoritative redwood-ip-list.csv for the staging environment so we can test before the Thursday window. Can you send that and a quick test plan/expected connection trace to validate NAT affinity for streams?

Alex
Network Architect — Summit Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 14:05:09 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private endpoint — minimal outbound allowlist and NAT behavior

Alex — quick answers and next steps: 

1) Certificates: For standard private deployments we use public certs with stable SNI. We do not issue customer-specific SAN certs by default. If Summit requires a dedicated certificate (mutual TLS or SAN-specific cert), we can scope it as an enterprise add-on and discuss deployment/rotation policies.

2) Staging IP CSV: attached (redwood-ip-list.csv) — it contains staging addresses and a note column with expected rotation windows. Use the staging FQDNs prefixed with "staging." (e.g., staging.stream.redwood-inference.com) for your tests.

3) Test plan (short):
   - Step 1: Allow egress TCP 443 to FQDNs in staging redwood-ip-list.csv from one test subnet.
   - Step 2: Start a streaming session using the Redwood SDK (we’ll provide a small script) and verify the WebSocket remains established for 20 minutes.
   - Step 3: Simulate NAT rotation (or cut over to a NAT with different outbound IP) and confirm the SDK reconnect logic recovers within your SLAs; we’ll log the reconnection timestamps.
   - Step 4: Confirm SNI shows staging.stream.redwood-inference.com in your proxy logs.

I attached the staging CSV and a one-page test script (also pushed to the shared Drive link above). If you’re comfortable reserving a small static pool for production, that’s our recommended final configuration.

I’m available Thu 10:00–11:00 PDT for a 30-minute NetOps verification call if you want to run tests with us.

— Rishi
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
